meta.title: QuietJar vs Ko-fi - the Ko-fi alternative that lives on your site
meta.description: Looking for a Ko-fi alternative? QuietJar keeps payment on your page instead of sending supporters to a hosted profile, with Google Pay, Apple Pay, and iDEAL built in.

ko-fi.title: The Ko-fi alternative that lives on your site.
ko-fi.intro: Ko-fi does a lot well: over a million creators, friendly hosted pages, payouts that land instantly. The question is what happens to your visitor after they decide to support you. On Ko-fi, they click your button, leave your site, and pay on Ko-fi's page. This alternative keeps the whole moment on your page, in your design.

sections.name: What you keep
sections.text: Ko-fi charges 5% on tips by default, and only drops that to 0% on a paid Gold plan (checked September 2026). Processing comes on top, at your own Stripe or PayPal rate. On a €10 tip that is €0.50 in platform fees plus €0.40 in card fees, so you keep €9.10. On a €100 donation you keep €93.25.
sections.text2: QuietJar's rate is 5% with a €0.50 minimum and nothing else: we pay the card fees ourselves, whichever method your supporter reaches for. On €10 you keep €9.50. On €100, €95.00. There is no monthly plan to buy your way out of the percentage, and no redirect to lose people on the way to the checkout.

sections.name: Goals
sections.text: Give the button a public target and a bar that fills toward it: hosting for the year, the next release, a new microphone. A concrete goal reframes the ask from a small favour to a shared plan, and lifts the amounts people choose. QuietJar reports +50% more conversions when a goal is set, and the bar sits in the widget on your page, right next to the payment.
sections.text2: Ko-fi has goals too, but they live on its hosted page. The visitor has to click away first, and by then some of them are gone.

sections.name: A dynamic image that keeps up
sections.text: A dynamic image that links straight into your donation panel. Drop it in your GitHub README or a newsletter, and it auto-updates with your goal progress, so the README you wrote in March still shows the right number in December. A static badge linking to a hosted page cannot do that.

sections.name: Google Pay and Apple Pay, on your site
sections.text: QuietJar puts Google Pay, Apple Pay, cards, and local methods like iDEAL and Bancontact directly on your page. Two taps on desktop, the same on mobile, and the checkout never shifts or stalls. Ko-fi's flow is PayPal-heavy, with no wallets or iDEAL, and it happens on Ko-fi's page, not yours.
